description: The five elder sisters each surface in turn and each names a different thing as the most beautiful -- the town and its bells, the sunset, the river and forests, the open sea, and the winter icebergs. The sequence occupies a large part of the opening and is what establishes the youngest sister's difference: her sisters are satisfied by a single visit and grow indifferent, while she is not. No unit represents it.
excerpt: As soon as the eldest was fifteen, she was allowed to rise to the surface of the ocean.

description: The grandmother's rule about rank and pain is stated as a general principle and is the story's first statement that its world charges for status. It bears directly on the later bargain, where the mermaid again accepts pain as a price.
excerpt: "Pride must suffer pain," replied the old lady.

description: After the transformation the sisters come to the surface nightly, and once the grandmother and the Sea King appear too, stretching out their hands but not venturing as near the land as the sisters do. This is the only evidence in the story of what her family does after she leaves, and it qualifies the witch's claim that she can never return to them.
excerpt: and once she saw in the distance her old grandmother, who had not been to the surface of the sea for many years, and the old Sea King, her father, with his crown on his head

description: The mermaid's singing voice is established as the finest of any on earth or in the sea before the witch demands it, at a court ball where the whole court applauds her. Without it the witch's valuation of the voice as the best thing she possesses is an assertion the reader cannot check.
excerpt: No one on earth has such a lovely voice as theirs. The little mermaid sang more sweetly than them all.

description: The witch gives the mermaid a defence against the polypi on the return journey -- a few drops of the potion would tear their fingers into a thousand pieces -- and it proves unnecessary because the polypi recoil from the draught itself. The detail closes the forest passage and shows the potion's power before it is drunk.
excerpt: throw over them a few drops of the potion, and their fingers will be torn into a thousand pieces

description: One unit carries both that the mermaid rises among the daughters of the air and the description of what those beings are. The fact of her survival and the nature of the beings she joins are independently checkable, and a reader may want the first without the second.
excerpt: "Among the daughters of the air," answered one of them.

description: The unit stating that the prince marries the neighboring king's daughter does not, on its own, carry that this same woman is the temple maiden from the rescue. That identity is what makes the ending a resolution rather than a coincidence, and it sits in a separate unit.
excerpt: "It was you," said the prince, "who saved my life when I lay dead on the beach,"
